raw_findings.verdict: On his own checklist Zach passes grit (6,195 solo commits over 210 days) and technical proficiency (the stale-checker story). Product sense is mixed: the wedge is plausible but stays a hypothesis. He falls short on traction (the 'Live' chips show that things run, not that anyone uses them) and on domain expertise (every customer test is planned, none has been run, so 'why weren't they able to get 10 people on the phone' goes unanswered). The pages hit three of Kyle's named AI-design tells. They open pinned to cyan on near-black. The Salvo block is undecoded jargon with false precision. The hero promises more than the EIR page admits ARCS can do. They also miss his one bar-lowerer, a visible long list of things shipped. Four fixes would turn this from 'another AI-built pitch' into 'a curious builder with receipts': default to OS or light theme, cut Salvo to one line, make five wedge calls and report the result, and add a dated list of things shipped. Keep the losing call record, the dated kill on ARCS and the 'Where the AI got it wrong' row exactly as they are.

resonates: The Bear row (Allium's strict filter: about $1.6M a month of real agent volume against 165M headline transactions) applies his own 'market cap is not activity' point one level down. It is the strongest row for him; keep it.

False negative, 'Agent commerce on card rails': on-chain volume undercounts because Visa and Mastercard run agent payments on tokenized cards. He sources Visa data himself and will read this as practitioner-aware.

The 1 in 3 call's resolution rule ('Announcements without an effective date do not count') is how someone who has shipped regulated products thinks. Rule-gated, dated and falsifiable, it matches his honesty register.
'My 85 to 90% crypto calls ran hot, so every call now ships with its falsifier and a lower number' mirrors how he publishes results that did not work out. Keep it verbatim.
The Inlier row ('An operator's agents paying its own services look like wash trades... I have not tested this') admits an untested point on the page itself, which he values.
EIR: 'Your stealth agentic payments company may already own this; I would ask first.' This is the right humility toward the portfolio. Keep it.
Keeping the whole ledger inside stablecoins and payments plays to the one area where he says he has unique insight, so he can actually judge it.
raw_findings.verdict: For Kyle as a Paxos practitioner, the crypto content is mostly credible, and two rows (Allium's strict filter, and agent payments on card rails undercounting on-chain) show real fluency in his activity-over-size lens. Fix one break before sending: the wedge rests on 'the send is final'. To the person who shipped freezable regulated stables, that is the naive version, and it puts the page's central claim on ground he has publicly rejected. Three smaller cracks repeat outsider framings he has written against. The L2 fee is labelled 'cost per payment' with ramps ignored. AML is framed as a large illicit-flow unknown. Coda's blocker is called compliance, when his own thesis says it is bank net interest income. The biggest missed opportunity is that the liability call is really his own footnote 25 (crypto payments must answer chargebacks and fraud liability) and his distribution-owns-the-rules thesis carried forward, and the page cites neither. Rewrite the wedge in freeze-and-intent terms, cite footnote 25 in the Trigger row, add a single 'who owns distribution' row, and cut the 30,000-run Salvo down to two plain lines. Then the ledger reads as built on his physics rather than as a better version of it.

raw_findings.verdict: Kyle would half-recognise himself here, and for this reader the problem is which half the page quotes back. The page never cites the words that make Zach the stage after his: his footnote that tuning the filter is the hardest part, and his line that AI is bad at judging significance. The kill-rate mirror (48 beliefs) has no denominator next to his measured 19 of 20. The pass recheck repeats his own "no right now" without credit. The prediction record, the one true echo of Mogg, never names Mogg. The material that would land is already on the page: the Hatch Desk line, the scored 2-of-9 calls, the pre-registered kill tests, and the "close the desk" exit. Fix by retiring the funnel headline in favour of the Hatch Desk line plus his footnote 4, crediting "no right now" and Mogg, stating the belief kill rate as a ratio, and putting the Salvo operator names into plain words. synthesis.verdict: Kyle would find a real builder in this family, but it doesn't yet mirror his gravity well. The substance is in his register: scored misses (2 hit, 6 missed of 9), a dated kill on ARCS itself, the stale-checker confession, activity-over-size rows (Allium filter, card-rails undercount) and priced kill tests. Six fixes come before any send. (1) Do not add the 'ripples in space and time / better physics' frame. He calls his own gravity sim a 'fun little' 'web based fidget spinner' the studio might use for its brand, and one-upping it is the single most expensive move available. The real mirror is his sentence that AI is bad at judging significance, plus the scored-calls row. (2) Rewrite the wedge. 'The send is final' contradicts his on-record point that regulated stables beat wires because they can be seized and frozen. Reframe it as freeze without an intent record. (3) Cut the Salvo block (BAR, COURT, Loki, KKL, Funhouse, '30,000 runs', a 90% band on a judgment) to two plain lines. It is the eval theatre he calls 'just a test framework'. (4) Stop pinning dark. The boot script ignores the OS, and cyan on near-black is the blue-on-black tell he names. Default to light or follow the OS, and drop 'ARCS FIELD OS'. (5) Retire the 'fills the funnel / de-risks the bottom' hero. He disowns funnel framing, and the claim outruns what EIR admits. Lead with his footnote 4 (the filter is the hard part). (6) Give the cold forward a top line: role, ask and a one-line ARCS definition. The crack-tier fixes would turn echoes of his work into homage rather than one-upmanship: cite footnote 25 on the liability call, credit 'no right now' and Mogg, put Coda's blocker as compliance versus net interest income, label the L2 fee as partial since ramps are excluded, state the belief kill rate as a ratio, swap the buzzword labels for plain verbs, cut the oak sentence, and move a dated list of shipped work up. If time allows, run 3 to 5 wedge calls and report the result. That answers his 'why weren't they able to get 10 people on the phone' directly.
